findings.title: Agent platform engineering reference architecture
findings.factual_summary: The guide frames production agent platforms as seven layers: orchestration, model inference, tools, memory, retrieval, control plane, and runtime. It also emphasizes delegated identity, tool caution, sandbox boundaries, trace-level observability, trajectory evaluation, model routing, and explicit governance controls.
findings.why_it_matters: Local practice pages may need to treat agent runtime design as a platform architecture concern rather than a prompt-only workflow. The useful downstream lens is how teams separate memory, retrieval, tools, policy, telemetry, and runtime ownership for coding agents.
findings.local_practice_implication: Consider downstream synthesis on agent platform boundaries, control-plane versus data-plane responsibilities, and trace evidence required for long-running AI-assisted development work.
findings.routing_note: Do not create local encyclopedia pages for the named platforms or protocols; route broad entity updates upstream.

findings.title: BMAD method guide for agent-driven development
findings.factual_summary: The guide describes BMAD as a spec-driven framework that converts planning, architecture, and implementation into documented agent workflows. It highlights cross-session drift, specialized roles, workflow phases, and context-engineered story files as the control mechanism.
findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki can use this as evidence for durable planning artifacts, role-specific agent instructions, and story-file handoffs as practice patterns for reducing cross-session context loss.
findings.local_practice_implication: Track whether local prompt-and-instruction pages distinguish durable repository memory, workflow templates, role prompts, and story-level context packages.
findings.routing_note: Keep BMAD background and product comparisons upstream; local use is the workflow pattern.

findings.title: Decision tree for prompts, AGENTS.md, skills, and MCP servers
findings.factual_summary: The post distinguishes one-off prompts, project or user AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md files, reusable skills, and MCP servers. Its decision tree uses reuse and reach: permanent guidance belongs in instruction files or skills, while new capabilities or hard-to-reach context belong behind MCP servers.
findings.why_it_matters: This directly supports local guidance on where durable agent instructions should live and when to escalate from prompt text to reusable skill or governed tool integration.
findings.local_practice_implication: A downstream leaf could encode the reuse-versus-reach rule for deciding among prompt, instruction file, skill, and MCP server.
findings.routing_note: MCP and product details remain upstream-owned; the local contribution is the customization decision rule.

findings.title: Recall-first AI code review guide
findings.factual_summary: The guide argues that AI-assisted code volume shifts the pull-request bottleneck to review capacity. It contrasts precision-first review with recall-first detection plus a filtering layer before developers see comments, and it frames missed production bugs as more costly than filtered false positives.
findings.why_it_matters: Local code-review practice pages may need to capture review-threshold tradeoffs, reviewer attention budgets, and benchmark-driven tuning rather than treating AI review as a single pass of comments.
findings.local_practice_implication: Record recall, precision, filtering, and human-review handoff as separate operating choices for AI code review workflows.
findings.routing_note: Product and benchmark entity coverage belongs upstream; local synthesis should focus on review practice.

findings.title: Scan-to-merge vulnerability remediation in AI pipelines
findings.factual_summary: The guide maps vulnerability remediation from scan through triage, prioritization, fix, and merge. It notes that dashboard-only findings create a developer handoff gap, AI-generated patches still need human verification, and reviewers must confirm regression tests and absence of new security issues.
findings.why_it_matters: This reinforces local practice for AI-assisted regression repair and security remediation: generated patches should enter normal PR evidence, severity gating, rescans, and human merge review rather than bypassing the development workflow.
findings.local_practice_implication: Potential downstream synthesis for scan-to-merge evidence requirements and remediation-agent gates.
findings.routing_note: Keep tool and standards background upstream; local scope is secure remediation workflow design.

findings.title: Freshness checks for CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md
findings.factual_summary: The post frames instruction files as operational memory that can become stale as libraries, incident decisions, and patterns change. It recommends provenance for rules, including creation reason, related files or incidents, affected code changes, and human confirmation dates.
findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki already treats durable instructions as project infrastructure; this source adds a freshness and provenance lens for avoiding stale agent policy.
findings.local_practice_implication: Consider a durable instruction-freshness checklist covering rule provenance, related files, last review, and stale-policy risk.
findings.routing_note: Do not duplicate product background; preserve the local rule-maintenance practice.

findings.title: Proof gates and release sign-off trails for remote agents
findings.factual_summary: The post argues that remote AI coding requires reproducible environments, test evidence, and human-readable release sign-off trails. It recommends templates defining environment, branch, permissions, commands, and expected evidence before a remote run starts.
findings.why_it_matters: This is directly relevant to local background-agent and automation practices: done criteria should include commands, diffs, screenshots, logs, test output, approvals, risks, and handoff state.
findings.local_practice_implication: Possible local synthesis for proof-gated remote-agent templates and release sign-off evidence.
findings.routing_note: Product names are upstream-owned; retain only workflow controls.

findings.title: Trusted MCP catalogs and verification checks
findings.factual_summary: The post treats MCP tool access as a supply-chain concern and calls for trusted tool catalogs, deterministic verification checks, visible routing decisions, and records of which server was invoked and what evidence it returned.
findings.why_it_matters: Local MCP practice pages may need explicit catalog trust, invocation evidence, and routing records as first-class workflow artifacts.
findings.local_practice_implication: Record MCP server approval, evidence capture, deterministic checks, and model-routing records as governed tool-call practice.
findings.routing_note: MCP broad coverage remains upstream-owned; local page should own governed MCP operation.

findings.title: MCP tool description poisoning governance warning
findings.factual_summary: The post summarizes a Microsoft warning about poisoned MCP tool descriptions, where hidden instructions in natural-language tool metadata can redirect an agent into data exfiltration. It describes re-approval triggers, description review, and tool metadata change control as governance needs.
findings.why_it_matters: This provides a concrete MCP governance failure mode for local tool-call practice: tool descriptions are part of the trusted execution surface and need review when they change.
findings.local_practice_implication: Potential downstream update for MCP server review checklists: treat tool descriptions, schema text, and prompt-like metadata as auditable supply-chain inputs.
findings.routing_note: Security incident and product background belongs upstream; local practice is governed MCP review.

findings.title: Agentic testing boundary taxonomy
findings.factual_summary: The post defines agentic testing as testing where an AI agent receives a natural-language goal, plans the test path, runs it against the application, observes runtime signals, and adapts without a hand-authored script underneath. It distinguishes agentic testing from AI-assisted test authoring and self-healing scripted tests.
findings.why_it_matters: Local verification pages can use this taxonomy to avoid conflating generated tests, maintained scripts, self-healing selectors, and fully agentic runtime test loops.
findings.local_practice_implication: Create or refresh a verification lens that classifies test ownership by who owns the path: human-authored script, AI-authored artifact, self-healing script, or agentic loop.
findings.routing_note: Product and tool pages belong upstream; local scope is test-loop taxonomy.

findings.title: Agent Studio roles served beside skills
findings.factual_summary: The post argues that skills and subagent definitions are complementary artifacts: skills describe reusable knowledge, while agents define roles, objectives, tool budgets, and return shape. It proposes serving both over the same endpoint with progressive disclosure and a moderation loop.
findings.why_it_matters: This supports local differentiation between reusable instructions and specialized worker roles in subagent-driven development.
findings.local_practice_implication: Potential downstream practice note: keep role definitions, tool budgets, and output contracts separate from procedural skill knowledge, even when served through the same discovery surface.
findings.routing_note: MCP endpoint design details are upstream technique territory; local use is the role-versus-skill operating boundary.

findings.title: Coordinator pattern for many coding-agent sessions
findings.factual_summary: The post describes an in-house coordination layer for coding-agent sessions with queues, callbacks, loops, handoffs, locks, session history, and cross-project messages. It separates coordinator sessions from fresh worker sessions and keeps AGENTS.md for repository-specific work rules while skills package repeatable workflows.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a practical solo-operator example of agent-session orchestration: recurring work benefits from stable coordinator state, callback contracts, and shared-resource locks rather than stuffing all context into one worker.
findings.local_practice_implication: Consider downstream synthesis for coordinator-worker loops, callback payloads, shared-resource locks, and separation of repo instructions from workflow skills.
findings.routing_note: Tool/product background is upstream-owned; local relevance is the orchestration practice.

findings.title: Compliance as code for AI-assisted development pull requests
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Article page shows Publication Date: July 4, 2026.
findings.factual_summary: The article argues that compliance rules drift when they live only in documentation and should be encoded as automated pull-request checks such as hardcoded-secret, RBAC, and idempotency checks. It links AI-assisted development velocity to a larger compliance review surface.
findings.why_it_matters: Local governance pages may need to connect AI-generated code velocity with executable compliance checks and audit-ready PR gates rather than policy documents alone.
findings.local_practice_implication: Track policy-as-code checks as part of AI-assisted development governance, especially when generated-code volume outpaces manual review.
findings.routing_note: Vendor background belongs upstream; local practice is PR-level compliance enforcement.
